(Range)': 'The sequence generator can only be used within an array constructor [].' With `..` out of the expression grammar the leftover token is the S0201 an unexpected token gets, which is what jsonata 2.2.2 reports here too.

A predicate is the filter operator '[ ... ]' (docs.jsonata.org/path-operators), not the array constructor the range operator is confined to, so a bare range is not legal there; the doubled form a[[1..3]] is. jsntrs answered [2,3,4] before jsntrs-uql; jsonata 2.2.2 rejects it as well.

SETTLED 2026-08-15 (jsntrs-2rp); was pinned as unresolved. docs.jsonata.org/numeric-operators says only 'The sequence generator can only be used within an array constructor []', which settles the bare cases but not this one — `[(1..3)]` IS within an array constructor, with the range nested inside a block. jsntrs's reading, adopted here and stated in docs/spec.md §4.9: the sequence generator must be an ELEMENT of the array constructor, one of the comma-separated expressions between [ and ], and a block '( ... )' is not an array constructor. The rule is IMPLIED, NOT STATED — the documentation's four examples all put the range directly in the constructor and it never addresses nesting. It was adopted because reading 'within an array constructor' as 'anywhere in the subtree' would also re-legalise [$sum(1..5)] and [a[1..3]], which that same sentence plainly excludes. jsonata 2.2.2 also answers S0202 here, but that is corroboration, not the reason. jsntrs answered [1,2,3] before jsntrs-uql.

jsntrs answered [2] before jsntrs-uql: `..` bound looser than `?`, so the range was read as the conditional's else branch. Recognising `..` only between two elements of the constructor makes the whole conditional the range's LHS, which is jsonata 2.2.2's reading too.
